perf.summary: Cache primes[j] in the inner loop and hoist the array load out of the product and modulo.
perf.currentCost: primes[j] is loaded multiple times per inner iteration (in the product, the store, and the i%primes[j] test). Each is a pointer load the JIT may not fully CSE across the long multiply.
perf.proposedChange: long pj = primes[j]; long prod = (long)i * pj; if (prod > n) break; minPrime[(int)prod] = (int)pj; if (i % pj == 0) break; Also AggressiveInlining is already present; consider hoisting (long)i once.
perf.rationale: Removes 2 redundant loads of primes[j] per inner iteration in the linear sieve's hottest loop (executed ~n times total), shortening the load/use dependency chain.
perf.risk: None — pj is loop-invariant within the iteration; pure CSE. Storing (int)pj instead of primes[j] is identical since primes[j] <= n fits int.

perf.summary: The i%primes[j] division can be avoided by tracking when primes[j] divides i via the minPrime array already being computed.
perf.currentCost: The inner loop does a 64/32-bit modulo (i % primes[j]) every iteration — a multi-cycle division on the hot path, executed ~n times.
perf.proposedChange: In a min-prime linear sieve, the standard break condition 'primes[j] divides i' is equivalent to 'primes[j] == minPrime[i]' once minPrime[i] is known (i's smallest prime factor). Replace the division-based test with an equality test: break when primes[j] == minPrime[i] (the loop only proceeds while primes[j] < minPrime[i]).
perf.rationale: Replaces an integer division (~20-40 cycles) with a register compare (1 cycle) in the innermost loop. minPrime[i] is already set for composite i during this pass (it was written when i was first crossed off), and for prime i minPrime[i]==i.
perf.risk: Requires that minPrime[i] is fully resolved before the inner loop runs for i — true in the linear sieve since i's smallest factor is set when it is first marked. Must verify ordering for prime i (set to i at top of iteration). If verified, exactly semantics-preserving and a real division elimination.
